design:
Mock approved by the operator (2026-11-10), built from real components fed mock state: `cd hub/ui && npx vite --config vite.mock.config.ts`, then http://localhost:5199/mock.html#tab/overview. Screenshots: testbed/ui-judge/setup-list/ (dark and light, 1440 and 960; dismissing on Overview and in settings; the rail hovered). Components on master (f9f10ee): hub/ui/src/components/overview/SetupList.tsx (SetupList, SetupCount), hub/ui/src/styles/setup.css, OverviewView's `setup` slot, Sidebar's `setupFor`. Mock state lives in hub/ui/mock/setupMock.ts.

Where it shows: Overview (one card above everything else), every Project settings section (above its heading; dismissed items listed only on Project with 'Show it again'), and the rail (a count beside the project's name, inside the row, naming the items on hover; on the compact rail a small count on the project's icon). The count is not a control of its own: the row opens Overview. It first sat at the row's end, where the hover actions cover it (operator, 2026-11-10).

What each item reads, all state the Hub already has:
- Folder found: the project's working directory exists.
- Git repository: is_repository. A missing main branch is not its own item: the Hub adopts one whenever it opens a repository.
- At least one agent: the roster, archived agents excluded.
- Every agent can run: launchability per provider (present = installed, authorized = logged in) for each agent's bound model.

Only dismissals are new state.

Build order against slice 2: setup-drive and setup-state share no file with slice 2 and use other agents, so they may run beside it. setup-ui must not start until slice 2's last task is done: it edits ProjectSettingsScreen.tsx and the committed bundle slice 2 rewrites (two branches rebuilding the bundle at once is F1140) and links to slice 2's Running page. The Hub cannot hold it for a task in another document (F1156), so if slice 2 is still running when setup-state is approved, the slice 5 build is stopped and pressed again once slice 2 finishes.

Hazard (Tier 2): the dismissal adds a migration; the operator's :8000 applies it on its next restart. The column defaults to nothing dismissed, so existing projects read as today.

open_questions.question: The rail mark: a number or a dot? Resolved: a number naming the items on hover, inside the row beside the name (operator, 2026-11-10).

Which items count? Resolved: folder found, git repository, at least one agent, every agent can run. Checks out (operator, 2026-11-10); instructions out (the Hub cannot see the files coding agents read on their own).
Can the operator dismiss an item? Resolved: yes (operator, 2026-11-10); the git item can be dismissed, the folder, agent and can-run items cannot.
Existing projects too? Resolved: all projects (operator, 2026-11-10).

problem: Operator, 2026-11-10: a new project gives no sign that it needs setting up, and no easy way to reach what does. Today the only hint is "No agents yet." on Overview (OverviewView.tsx:352). Slice 4 shipped what a list can link to: 'Make this a git repository' (MakeRepositoryOffer.tsx exports a `make-repository` anchor for this list). Opening a repository already adopts its main branch on its own (projects.py `_adopt_detected_main_branch`), so a missing main branch only happens without git. The Hub already knows, per provider, whether its coding agent is installed and logged in (`/runners/launchability-by-provider`: present, authorized, runnable), and whether the project's folder is still where it was bound (General → Folder: Available / Missing; the rail's 'Directory unavailable' mark).

requirements.rationale: Each is something without which work does not happen or is not isolated, and each is something the Hub can tell for itself. Checks and instructions were left out: a starting project may have no checks (operator, 2026-11-10), and the Hub cannot see the instruction files coding agents read on their own.
requirements.statement: A project's set-up list holds exactly these items, each shown only while it is not met: its folder is found where it was bound; its folder is a git repository; it has at least one agent that is not archived; every agent that is not archived can run, meaning its model's coding agent is installed and logged in on this machine (one item per agent that cannot).

Each item opens what resolves it: a missing folder opens Project settings → Project at its 'Locate project' field; no repository opens the 'Make this a git repository' action; no agent opens adding an agent; an agent that cannot run names that agent and why (not installed, or not logged in), and opens its Running → Model.

requirements.rationale: A scratch folder may deliberately have no git, and an item that can never clear teaches the operator to ignore the mark. Without a folder, an agent, or an agent that runs, nothing works at all, so those cannot be waved away.
requirements.statement: The operator can dismiss the git repository item for a project with 'Not for this project', after which it is not shown in any of the three places and the dismissal survives a Hub restart; a dismissed item is listed in Project settings → Project with a way to show it again. The folder, agent and can-run items cannot be dismissed.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-10: the count first sat where the row's hover actions appear and was covered by them.
requirements.statement: While any item is shown, the list appears at the top of the project's Overview and at the top of every Project settings section, and the project's row in the rail carries a count of the items left beside its name, naming them on hover, never covered by the row's hover actions; the row opens the project's Overview. When none is shown, none of the three appears.
The list is worked out for every project, including those created before this change, from the project's current state and nothing recorded at its creation.

An item disappears without a reload once what it names is resolved, in the same session it was resolved in: making the repository, adding an agent, choosing a model that can run, or locating the folder.
A project with a found folder, a git repository, and only agents that can run shows no list and no count; this repository on the operator's Hub is such a project.

in_scope: The four conditions that make a project not ready: folder found, a git repository, at least one agent, every agent able to run
The list on Overview, a count on the project in the rail, and the list in project settings
Each item linking to the setting or action that resolves it
Dismissing the repository item, and undoing that
Every project, including those already in use
non_goals: Checks: a project just starting may have none (operator, 2026-11-10)
Instructions: the Hub cannot tell whether an agent has them, since each coding agent reads its own file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) without the Hub
Charters, permissions, budgets, landing and anything else that has a working default
Doing the set-up for the operator: each item links to it
A wizard or forced flow on project creation
New Hub settings beyond remembering what was dismissed

summary: A project that cannot yet do its work says so on Overview, in the rail and in settings. It lists what it still needs, and each item opens the setting or action that resolves it. The list goes away once every item is done or dismissed.
